note: The narration, as spoken in the final takes (public/audio/vo-0N.mp3, the founder's cloned voice; launch/VOICEOVER.md). One file per line; the scratch voice (public/audio/scratch, Windows text-to-speech) only stands in when a take is missing. lines.scene: a sentence typed to an agent, a shop appears
lines.text: This is Awning. You tell your AI agent one sentence, and it opens a real business that people, and other AI agents, can buy from.

Starting a small business still means a website, a domain, a checkout. And there's a new kind of customer now: AI agents with wallets. In a September audit of two hundred retailers, only thirty-eight could take their money.

lines.scene: Claude drafts Ridge Roast, the preview
lines.text: Here's Ridge Roast, a coffee roaster in Accra. Awning names it, prices the offers, checks real domains, and puts up a private preview. Nothing is paid yet.

lines.scene: PayBox approval, the shop goes live
lines.text: One approval in PayBox, and Ridge Roast is open. On its own domain. A real one.

lines.scene: a fresh chat finds the shop and buys a tasting, the receipt prints
lines.text: Now, in a fresh chat, an agent goes shopping for a coffee tasting in Accra. It finds Ridge Roast on its own. Five dollars in USDC, one approval, paid straight to the owner's wallet. Ridge Roast's first customer was an AI.

lines.scene: owner adds an offer, checks orders, the directory, the live feed
lines.text: The owner runs the shop from the same chat: add a subscription box, check the orders. Every shop is listed where any agent can find it, and every sale lands on a public receipt you can check on chain.

Under the hood, the plugin never moves money. It proposes, and PayBox asks you. Awning only takes the payment after the shop is live, so if anything fails, you're not charged. Sales go straight to the owner's wallet. Awning never holds them.
Every business on Awning is born agent-payable.
One sentence. One approval. Open yours at awning dot S-H.
